Name: Simple Tool Belt 2 (New Update)
Author: Xsyy
Description:
[b]Simple Tool Belt[/b]
Keep your everyday tools together in one backpack slot. Choose a tool through a compact quick tray, or enable Smart Switching to temporarily use the right stored tool for your target.
Your tools keep their upgrades, enchantments, water and mod data.

[b]Features[/b]
[list]
[*]Eight tool slots, with one tool per category.[/*]
[*]Supports Axe, Pickaxe, Hoe, Watering Can, Scythe, Milk Pail, Shears and Weapon.[/*]
[*]Optional Smart Switching, off by default.[/*]
[*]A small tool badge shows your currently selected belt tool.[/*]
[*]Keyboard, mouse and controller support.[/*]
[*]Support for all 12 built-in game languages.[/*]
[*]Optional Generic Mod Config Menu support.[/*]
[/list]Fishing rods and pans cannot be stored. The Weapon category accepts a melee weapon or slingshot.

[b]How to obtain[/b]
Use Clint’s tool-upgrade service, then look for his letter the following morning. The Simple Tool Belt becomes available at his normal shop for [b]10,000g[/b].
All eight slots are included. Existing owners keep their belt and previously earned unlocks.

[b]Using the belt[/b]
Right-click the belt in your backpack to manage its contents. You can also open it through the belt shortcut beside the normal player menu.
Click an eligible backpack tool to store it. Click two belt positions to swap them, or right-click a stored tool to return it to your backpack.
Select the belt in your hotbar and press [b]Action[/b]—right-click by default—to open the [b]2 × 4 quick tray[/b] when nothing is available to interact with. Choose a tool by clicking it or using your first eight hotbar keys.
Use the selected tool with your normal [b]Use Tool[/b] control. Returning to the belt remembers your last selected position.

[b]Smart Switching[/b]
Enable Smart Switching in the belt’s management screen. Carry the belt and perform a normal tool action to temporarily borrow the appropriate stored tool.
Examples:
[list]
[*]Target a rock to use your Pickaxe.[/*]
[*]Target a tree to use your Axe.[/*]
[*]Target a dry planted crop to use your Watering Can.[/*]
[*]Target a ready cow or goat to use your Milk Pail.[/*]
[*]Target a ready sheep to use your Shears.[/*]
[*]Target a monster to use your Weapon.[/*]
[/list]Your previous selection returns when the action finishes—even if you had another tool selected. Charged watering keeps the Watering Can active through charging, release and the watering animation.
If you change your selection manually, the belt respects your choice. Nothing activates simply because you walk near a target.

[b]Normal interactions still work[/b]
While the belt is selected, Action prioritizes normal interactions such as opening chests, talking to villagers, petting animals, using doors and collecting from machines.
The quick tray opens only when the world interaction is unhandled.

[b]Controller support[/b]
Use the D-pad or left stick to navigate the quick tray, [b]A[/b] to choose a position and [b]B[/b] to close it.
In the management screen, [b]A[/b] stores or reorders tools, [b]X[/b] withdraws them, and shoulder buttons change backpack pages.

[b]Upgrading your tools[/b]
Withdraw a tool to your backpack before taking it to Clint or using the forge. After upgrading or enchanting it, put it back into the belt.

[b]Lost your belt?[/b]
Tools remain saved separately from the physical belt. After the mod confirms the belt is missing across two day-end checks, Clint sends a recovery letter. Read it, then collect a replacement from his shop for free.
The replacement reconnects to your stored tools and invalidates the old belt.

[b]Updating from an older version[/b]
Replace your existing SimpleToolBelt folder with the new version.
Previously stored fishing rods, pans and duplicate tool categories return to your backpack. If your backpack is full, they remain safely saved until space becomes available.

[b]Compatibility[/b]
Compatible modded tools based on the supported game tool categories can be stored. Smart Switching depends on recognizable tool and target behavior, so unusual custom interactions may require manual selection.
All players in multiplayer should use the same version.

[b]Installation[/b]
Requires [b]Stardew Valley 1.6.15+[/b] and [b]SMAPI 4.2+[/b].
Extract the SimpleToolBelt folder into your Mods folder and launch the game through SMAPI.
Generic Mod Config Menu is optional. Smart Switching can be toggled directly in the belt menu without it.
Withdraw all stored tools before uninstalling the mod.
